summary.text: 本 is built from 木, a tree, and a lower mark indicating its root. Root is the proposed original meaning; later recorded uses include base, foundation, source, and basis, though their precise development is unclear.

formation.text: Ideographic: 木 depicts a tree, and a mark at its lower part indicates the root. The transmitted explanations differ on whether that mark is 一 or 丅.

components.text: 木 depicts the tree, providing the plant context for the root indication. In this construction it is pictorial and semantic, not phonetic.
The visible current graph has 一 as its lower stroke, indicating the tree’s root. Historical analyses disagree on whether the mark was 一 or 丅, and no sequence between these readings is established.

history.text: The selected seal-script-style illustration shows a tree-like form crossed by a lower horizontal mark. It is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact. Early inscriptional evidence remains unsettled: one record lists a bronze example that another does not display, and a proposed oracle-bone precursor is disputed; these do not establish a secure sequence of graphic change.

The transmitted Shuowen explanation describes 木 with a lower mark; its readings differ on whether that mark is 一 or 丅. A separate account describes a dot in Western Zhou forms and a short horizontal stroke in Warring States forms, without establishing how those forms relate to the competing Shuowen readings.

One account describes the Shuowen ancient form as 木 above three root-like marks. It separately reports that some Warring States variants use 白 to depict a tree pit; the two proposals do not establish a sequence between them.

uncertainties.text: The earliest inscriptional form and date remain unresolved. The reported bronze graph’s reading and meaning are unsettled, and the proposed oracle-bone identification is disputed.
Root, trunk, base, foundation, source, and basis are recorded meanings, but the precise pathways from the root sense to abstract, documentary, or other uses are not established.

The account of the Shuowen ancient form leaves the three root-like marks unidentified; the proposed Warring States tree-pit form does not establish their identity or a graphic relationship between the two forms.

senses.text: The transmitted Shuowen explanation and a cited Book of Odes passage associate 本 with a plant’s root or lower part. The passage’s composition date is unresolved, and these sources do not establish this as the earliest attested use.
A cited Zhuangzi passage records 本 for a tree trunk. Its first occurrence and precise relation to the root sense are undated.
Current dictionary definitions include root, origin, source, and basis. Older cited examples also record foundation uses, but they do not date when this sense arose.
Current dictionary entries list source, cause, and basis among 本’s meanings. Their precise development from the root or foundation sense and their first occurrence dates are not established.
Current definitions include root, origin, source, and basis; this list does not establish their chronology.

A Japanese lexical account proposes that 本 meaning ‘original’ or ‘source’ came to refer first to an exemplar manuscript and then to books generally. This proposed Japanese word history is separate from the documented Chinese senses and from the character’s graphic origin.

developments.text: Both root and foundation are documented; an extension from a plant’s base to a figurative basis is plausible, though its transition and chronology are not demonstrated.
Source and basis uses are recorded alongside foundation, but the precise development and dates are not shown.

limitations.text: The cited literary passages and dictionary entries document uses but do not establish exact first-attestation dates or a complete chronology of semantic development.
The earliest archaeological attestation is unresolved, as is the reading of the reported bronze example.

items.period: Han Shuowen seal-script model; digital image uploaded 2016
items.caption: This seal-script-style redraw shows a tree-like form with a horizontal mark crossing its lower trunk. It illustrates the traditional Shuowen analysis of 本 as 木 with a mark below indicating the root; it does not resolve the competing readings of that mark as 一 or 丅.
items.alt: Black seal-script-style graph on white: an upper tree-like form with a horizontal line crossing its lower trunk.
items.selection_reason: The crossing mark makes the root-indicator explanation visible. The image is a modern redraw and does not establish the earlier inscriptional forms or settle the competing 一 and 丅 analyses.

evidence.field: 形義通解: formation and semantic development
evidence.text: The entry analyzes 本 as 木 plus 一, with the mark indicating the lower part of a plant; it gives the original sense as plant root. It cites 說文解字 and 呂氏春秋·辯土 (with Gao You's note “本，根也”), then records extensions to the base/end of an elongated object, a tree trunk, a foundation or principal part, source/cause, basis/evidence, manuscript draft, and a classifier. evidence.text: The entry distinguishes two transmitted Shuowen readings: the Daxu text analyzes 木 plus 一 below it; Duan Yucai's annotated text instead reads 木 plus 丅. It also notes that 夲 has an independent sense/pronunciation (tāo, rapid advance) although it has also served as a popular written variant of 本. evidence.source: Du Qingyu (杜清雨), Lingnan Journal of Chinese Studies
evidence.text: A 2025 article argues that a disputed oracle-bone graph is an early form of 本 and interprets it in sacrificial inscriptions as a human torso or lower body, possibly connected with dismemberment or waist execution. Its abstract reports other identifications as 垂, 叕, and 瓜 and argues they have shortcomings. This is a recent disputed proposal, not settled evidence that the received tree-root graph is attested in oracle-bone writing.

evidence.source: 漢字教育士ひろりんの書斎
evidence.field: 2018 discussion: early attestation and competing structure
evidence.text: The author reports finding no oracle-bone 本 in the references checked and only a rare Western Zhou bronze example on the vessel called 本鼎; the author treats it as likely a maker's name, so its word meaning is uncertain. The article notes the transmitted Shuowen analysis 木 plus 一, contrasted with Duan Yucai's 木 plus the seal form of 下, and reports that both readings give a lower/tree-related meaning. This is a secondary discussion and an explicit challenge to treating the bronze graph as secure semantic evidence.
evidence.title: 本という字の謎

evidence.source: 漢字教育士ひろりんの書斎, quoting 詩經 and 論語
evidence.text: The page quotes 詩經·大雅·蕩 “枝葉未有害，本實先撥” and explains 本 as root in context; it also quotes 論語·學而 “君子務本，本立而道生” in a foundation sense. These are transmitted-text attestations, not archaeological inscriptions. The page does not establish exact composition dates for the passages, so no precise earliest date is assigned here.
evidence.title: 本という字の謎

evidence.source: Wiktionary
evidence.text: The entry gives modern Standard Mandarin běn (Pinyin), Cantonese bun2 (Jyutping, Guangzhou–Hong Kong), Middle Chinese pwonX (Baxter notation; also gives Guangyun fanqie 布忖), Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *C.pˤə[n]ʔ, and Zhengzhang Shangfang *pɯːnʔ. These are readings/reconstructions of 本, not of 木 or 一 as a proposed phonetic element. They support a descriptive sound history for 本 but do not make either component phonetic.

evidence.text: The author reports finding no oracle-bone 本 in the references checked and only a rare Western Zhou bronze example on the vessel called 本鼎; the author treats it as likely a maker's name, so its word meaning is uncertain. The article notes the transmitted Shuowen analysis 木 plus 一, contrasted with Duan Yucai's 木 plus the seal form of 下, and reports that both readings give a lower/tree-related meaning. This is a secondary discussion and an explicit challenge to treating the bronze graph as secure semantic evidence.
evidence.title: 本という字の謎

evidence.source: 漢字教育士ひろりんの書斎, quoting 詩經 and 論語
evidence.text: The page quotes 詩經·大雅·蕩 “枝葉未有害，本實先撥” and explains 本 as root in context; it also quotes 論語·學而 “君子務本，本立而道生” in a foundation sense. These are transmitted-text attestations, not archaeological inscriptions. The page does not establish exact composition dates for the passages, so no precise earliest date is assigned here.
evidence.title: 本という字の謎

evidence.source: Wiktionary
evidence.text: The entry gives modern Standard Mandarin běn (Pinyin), Cantonese bun2 (Jyutping, Guangzhou–Hong Kong), Middle Chinese pwonX (Baxter notation; also gives Guangyun fanqie 布忖), Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *C.pˤə[n]ʔ, and Zhengzhang Shangfang *pɯːnʔ. These are readings/reconstructions of 本, not of 木 or 一 as a proposed phonetic element. They support a descriptive sound history for 本 but do not make either component phonetic.
evidence.title: 本 - Wiktionary

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Revised Mandarin Chinese Dictionary
evidence.field: Historical lexical examples and modern reading
evidence.text: The entry gives běn and quotes Shuowen “木下曰本,” 呂氏春秋·士容論·辯士 with Han commentator Gao You glossing 本 as root, and 論語·學而 “君子務本，本立而道生.” It separately lists book/document, capital, manuscript, basis, original, current, and self/own-side uses. These citations provide attestations in named works but do not establish when each sense first arose.
evidence.title: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》 — 本

evidence.source: Chinese Text Project
evidence.field: Search result for 詩經·大雅·蕩
evidence.text: Search results identify the passage “枝葉未有害、本實先撥” in 詩經·大雅·蕩. The page itself could not be opened in this research session, so this is recorded only as a search-result lead, not as inspected source-page evidence.
evidence.title: Book of Poetry: Greater Odes, Decade of Dang: Dang

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Small Seal Script Database
evidence.field: 字形演變: bronze form and formation note
evidence.text: The 本 record lists a bronze-inscription example under 集成02081 and describes 本 as 木 with a semantic indicator at the root, meaning root/base. It does not list an oracle-bone form on this page; that omission alone does not establish non-attestation.
evidence.title: 漢字「本」：字形演變

evidence.source: CUHK Humanum 漢語多功能字庫
evidence.field: 形義通解; 字形資料; 說文 and 廣韻 records
evidence.text: The entry interprets 本 as 木 plus 一, with 一 marking the lower part, and gives the original sense as plant root. It quotes Shuowen 木下曰本 and Lüshi Chunqiu with Gao You's root gloss. It displays one small-seal example, seven manuscript forms and one other form, with no examples displayed in its bronze or oracle slots. It gives Guangyun fanqie 布忖. The senses it lists include the base of a long object, trunk, foundation, source/cause, basis, draft and classifier; their order is not a chronology.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明; 釋義
evidence.text: The entry distinguishes the Daxu Shuowen reading 木 plus 一 below from Duan Yucai's annotated reading 木 plus 丅. It says 夲 has its own reading ㄊㄠ and sense ‘rapid advance,’ while also being a common written variant of 本; this does not establish that 夲 is a chronological ancestor of 本. It cites the Book of Odes for a plant's lower part/root, Zhuangzi for trunk, and the Book of Documents and Analects for foundation, alongside later cited senses. The citations identify transmitted works but do not date when each sense first arose.
evidence.title: Ministry of Education 《Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants》2024

evidence.source: Wikimedia Commons
evidence.text: Commons describes 本-seal.svg as a modern digital vector drawing of 本 in Shuowen seal-script style, points to Sinica, Chinese Etymology and CUHK among its reference sources, and marks the SVG representation public domain. It is a modern redraw, not a photograph or facsimile of an ancient artifact.
evidence.title: File:本-seal.svg

evidence.source: Japanese Wiktionary
evidence.field: 字源; Japanese book sense etymology
evidence.text: The entry analyzes 本 as an indicative graph marking the root portion of 木 and gives a reconstructed Han word for root. Separately, for the Japanese reading ホン meaning ‘book,’ it describes a development from 本 meaning ‘original/source’ to an exemplar manuscript and then books generally, citing Makura no Sōshi. This is a Japanese lexical semantic account, not evidence for the ancient Chinese graphic formation.
evidence.title: 本 - ウィクショナリー日本語版

evidence.source: 李學勤主編《字源》
evidence.field: 本 entry; formation, glyph sequence and semantic examples; PDF p. 516, printed p. 503; scan /home/catalin/hanzi-etymology-books/research-ocr/ziyuan-full/page-0516/source.png (file SHA-256 f732cc6b3e3988c9455fe2aa8c420cafa0adbc24c01aa76fb742a9f67a1df5b4)
evidence.text: The scanned 本 headword describes the graph as 指事. It says Western Zhou forms add a dot at the part of 木 representing the tree root, and Warring States forms change the dot to a short horizontal stroke. It describes the Shuowen ancient form as 木 above three root-like marks; some Warring States variants use 白 to represent a tree pit. It gives the original meaning as tree root, quotes 《国语·晋语一》 “伐木不自其本，必复生,” and records further uses for plant stem/trunk and figurative fundamental or important matters, including contrast with 末 and an agriculture sense. This is one source’s account; the early graph sequence and the cited works’ composition dates are not independently established here.
evidence.title: 字源, 李學勤主編, 2012 (edition catalogue lookup)

evidence.source: 中央研究院小學堂漢字形體演變資料庫
evidence.text: The page lists a bronze inscription form under 集成02081 and characterizes 本 as 木 with an added indicative mark at the root, meaning root/base. It displays no oracle-bone section for 本. This record supports a bronze-form listing and its stated analysis, but its missing oracle-bone listing alone does not establish non-attestation.
evidence.title: 漢字「本」：字形演變

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明; 釋義
evidence.text: The entry reports two transmitted Shuowen readings: the Daxu text has 木 with 一 below it, while Duan Yucai's annotated text reads 木 with 丅. It says the regular-script form is written with a short horizontal stroke below 木. It also notes 夲 has an independent reading and meaning ‘rapid advance’ while serving as a common written variant of 本; this does not establish a chronological ancestor relation. Its citations include the Odes for the plant’s lower part/root, Zhuangzi for trunk, and Documents/Analects for foundation. The citations identify examples but do not themselves establish when each sense arose.
evidence.title: Ministry of Education 《Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants》 — 本

evidence.source: CUHK Humanum 漢語多功能字庫
evidence.field: 形義通解; 《說文》 and cited lexical examples
evidence.text: The entry analyzes 本 as 木 plus 一 and gives ‘root of plants/trees’ as the original meaning; it cites Shuowen and Lüshi Chunqiu with Gao You’s gloss 本，根也. It separately records the base of an elongated object, plant trunk, foundation/main body, source/cause, evidence/basis, manuscript draft and classifier uses. The page presents these as meanings with examples, not a dated chronology of semantic change.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 本

evidence.source: 杜清雨 (Qingyu Du), 嶺南學報
evidence.field: Abstract; competing oracle-bone interpretation; vol. 23, pp. 125–139
evidence.text: The article proposes that a disputed oracle-bone graph is the initial form of 本 and interprets it in sacrificial inscriptions as a human torso or lower body, possibly related to dismemberment or waist execution. Its abstract reports competing readings 垂, 叕 and 瓜. This is a disputed proposal, not settled proof that the received tree-root graph is attested in oracle-bone writing.
evidence.title: 甲骨文“本”字試解 / An explanation of the character in Oracle Bone Inscription

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Revised Mandarin Chinese Dictionary
evidence.text: The entry gives běn and cites Shuowen 木下曰本, Lüshi Chunqiu with Gao You’s gloss 本，根也, and Analects 君子務本，本立而道生. It separately records source/origin, capital, funds, books, scripts, classifiers and other uses. This documents cited examples and current lexical categories, not a full chronology of their development.
evidence.title: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》 — 本

evidence.source: 李學勤主編《字源》, 天津古籍出版社, 2012, ISBN 978-7-5528-0069-2; PDF p. 516, printed p. 503; directly inspected attached scan `/home/catalin/hanzi-etymology-books/research-ocr/ziyuan-full/page-0516/source.png` (attachment SHA-256 f732cc6b3e3988c9455fe2aa8c420cafa0adbc24c01aa76fb742a9f67a1df5b4; decoded RGB pixel SHA-256 76e89fb3390b16e589bbeacf1ff99ba36437a957df3969860a7df252c8f0de50)
evidence.field: 本 headword, graph-history discussion, paragraph below the glyph sequence
evidence.text: In its account of the graph sequence under 本, 字源 describes the Shuowen ancient form as 木 above three root-like marks. It separately says that some Warring States forms use 白 to depict a tree pit. These are two distinct proposals in this book’s account; the passage does not establish a sequence between them. The uncommon marks in the Shuowen ancient-form sample are left unidentified.

context.provenance: Local imported excerpts supplemented by the external research records and audit below. External evidence records are paraphrases of the cited pages, accessed 2026-09-26.
editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

items.period: Han Shuowen seal-script model; digital image uploaded 2016
items.caption: This seal-script-style redraw shows a tree-like form with a horizontal mark crossing its lower trunk. It illustrates the traditional Shuowen analysis of 本 as 木 with a mark below indicating the root; it does not resolve the competing readings of that mark as 一 or 丅.
items.alt: Black seal-script-style graph on white: an upper tree-like form with a horizontal line crossing its lower trunk.
items.selection_reason: The crossing mark makes the root-indicator explanation visible. The image is a modern redraw and does not establish the earlier inscriptional forms or settle the competing 一 and 丅 analyses.
items.rights: Public domain release stated on Commons file page.

limitations.text: This is a modern redraw of a seal-script-style form, not an ancient artifact. 本’s earliest inscriptional form and date remain unsettled: a bronze example is listed by one source but not displayed by another, and a proposed oracle-bone identification is disputed.

gaps: The exact early relationship between the root meaning and later abstract senses is not established by the inspected pages; dictionaries supply citations and glosses rather than dated semantic pathways.
Sinica lists a bronze inscription example (集成02081), while CUHK's current page displays no bronze example. The specific inscription's reading and sense were not independently resolved in this search.

A disputed 2025 proposal in the supplied dossier identifies an oracle-bone graph as an ancestor of 本, but the current independent search did not inspect that paper; oracle-bone status remains unresolved.
No pronunciation comparison for 木 or 一 is needed to establish their semantic roles here; inspected accounts treat both as semantic, not phonetic, components. No phonetic series is evidenced.

The Wikimedia seal image is a modern redraw. The directly linked bronze variant could not be opened due to cache failure, so it is not proposed as an image candidate. No actual image pixels were inspected.
Direct-image URL retrieval for the Commons SVG failed in the web tool; the description page supplied candidate identity and rights metadata, not visual confirmation.
